title: Home Oxygen Therapy Records Register Standard: One Open Oxygen Record per Patient
content:
# One Open Oxygen Record per Patient — Home Oxygen Therapy

**Standard.** A patient holds at most 1 open Home Oxygen Therapy record. An oxygen record is open in any status other than returned, cancelled or lifetime ended. A different system class is furnished by changing the class on the existing record, never by opening a second one.

**Condition for opening a record.** A new oxygen record is opened only when no oxygen record of the patient is order received, an active rental, suspended or payment cap reached. A replacement election under the useful-lifetime rule closes the old record before the new one is opened.

## Basis of the judgement

- The judgement rests on the system record: the oxygen records held under the patient, and the status each of them shows, are read before a new record is opened.
- The correlation is by patient: every oxygen record of the same patient is considered, whatever its system class.

## Status table

| Status of an existing oxygen record of the patient | Counts as open | A new oxygen record may be opened while it stands |
|---|---|---|
| order received | yes | no |
| active rental | yes | no |
| suspended | yes | no |
| payment cap reached | yes | no |
| returned | no | — |
| cancelled | no | — |
| lifetime ended | no | — |

A new record may be opened only when none of the patient's oxygen records is in one of the first four statuses.

## Cases (hypothetical)

1. A patient's only Home Oxygen Therapy record is returned. No record of the patient is in an open status, so a new record may be opened.
2. A patient's record is suspended and a different system class is ordered. The record is open; the new class is furnished by changing the class on the existing record, not by opening a second record.
3. A patient's record is payment cap reached and the patient makes a replacement election under the useful-lifetime rule. The election closes the old record first; the new record is then opened.
